case_name: V.N. Sunanda Reddy & Ors. v State Of Andhra Pradesh & Ors.
facts: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act, 1966 states that Telugu shall be the official language of the State.

In 1970, the State Government wrote to several other State Governments to ascertain whether any weightage or preference was given to candidates who had studied in the respective regional languages in the matter of recruitment to public posts.

The Government of Kerala, Pondicherry, Tripura, Haryana, Goa, Daman and Diu, Rajasthan, Kohima, Assam, Himachal Pradesh, West Bengal, Punjab, Gujarat, and Bihar replied that no such preference or weightage was given in the process of recruitment.
In some States, knowledge of regional language was essential for appointment while in some states they were required to pass the language test within a fixed period after appointment.
issues: Whether the State Government of Andhra Pradesh was justified in promulgating the rules under which it was provided that candidates seeking appointment to the posts who had obtained basic educational qualifications prescribed for direct recruitment governing such posts through the Telugu medium shall be given weightage in the matter of selection to such posts by awarding them five per cent of the total aggregate maximum marks in the relevant competitive examination held by the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission for recruitment to such posts.
petitioner_arguments: The provision of weightage to Telugu medium candidates only would be arbitrary and discriminatory and would be destructive of the concept of selection on pure merits.

Even if Telugu is the official language, once a candidate is recruited from the open market as per the relevant rules before he is confirmed in service and before he is entitled to earn an increment in service, he is required to pass the Telugu language examination.
respondent_arguments: The provision of weightage to Telugu medium candidates only would have no real nexus to the object sought to be achieved and would be counter productive as more meritorious students even though having secured more marks in the aggregate in the competitive test would be elbowed out by those standing far behind in the queue only on the specious plea that they have passed the qualifying examination in the Telugu medium.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the provision of weightage to Telugu medium candidates only was not violative of the Constitutional provisions of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.

The Court noted that the object of securing efficiency in administration would be satisfied by requiring a candidate to pass the Telugu language examination after he is recruited from the open market as per the relevant rules.
holding: The appeals were allowed and the impugned G.O. was upheld.
The Court held that the provision of weightage to Telugu medium candidates only was not violative of the Constitutional provisions of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
